10.1051/aacus/2026008.note: Examined the methods, field evaluation and discussion. Uses an eight-MEMS-microphone array, an ESP32-S3 acquisition component and separate processing, with TDOA and a classifier. Cite to delimit the application landscape, not to claim that a simulated three-microphone RMSE beats a field experiment. The full text gives inconsistent descriptions of the timing platform (Raspberry Pi versus an Intel platform); do not lift its latency numbers into a quantitative comparison without clarification. Its existence also does not validate the present firmware.

10.1051/aacus/2026043.note: Examined the numerical setup, convergence checks, analytical reference comparison and conclusions. This Technical & Applied study of force-radiation-mode control is computational, with experimental work left for the future. It directly contradicts the old local assumption that new measurements are universally mandatory for this journal. The lesson is to supply independent verification and a useful acoustic result, not to treat simulation alone as sufficient novelty.

10.1051/aacus/2026049.note: Examined the simulation and optimization methods and deployment limitations. Uses modal and finite-element descriptions for sparse estimation/control of wall-scattered pressure, with model parameters informed by measurements. Useful for structuring an accuracy-versus-sensor/computation study and distinguishing proposed control performance from achieved hardware performance. It should not be described as wholly measurement-free.

10.1051/aacus/2026048.note: Examined the abstract, verification/validation structure and conclusions. The collaborative impedance benchmark distinguishes implementation mistakes, numerical convergence, physical-model assumptions, specimen differences and operator variability. Iterative comparison exposed errors before final results agreed. Recommends simple analytical reference cases, resolution refinement, explicit uncertainties and shared raw data/post-processing. Adopt that separation for rounded arrivals, curvature, transient handling and reverberation; agreement between two outputs generated by the same model is not independent physical validation.

10.1051/aacus/2026068.note: Examined the dataset description, simulation workflow, validation discussion and limitations. FLOW-01 provides experimental cylinder-flow data plus a simplified open-source two-dimensional workflow intended to run on ordinary computers. It explicitly acknowledges missing three-dimensional turbulent structure and corrections used for comparison. The transferable contribution is a standardized case with usable metadata and honest fidelity limits. Your existing recordings cannot serve as its equivalent ground-truth localization dataset.

10.1051/aacus/2025011.note: Examined calibration results and discussion. Constrained least-squares and maximum-likelihood estimates seek both an RT match and more plausible material parameters; uncertainty and initial knowledge affect success. The geometrical-acoustics case studies show that Sabine-based targets can differ from the simulator's realized T20 and that improving one metric can worsen another. In your study, report realized RIR decay and direct/early/late characteristics rather than labeling a room only by the requested RT60. This is an analogy in validation practice, not a proposed calibration algorithm to copy.

10.1051/aacus/2024062.note: Examined abstract, technical/perceptual evaluation and conclusions. The RAZR scattering approximations are evaluated through echo-density evolution and listening comparisons with measured rooms; perceptual benefits depend on the stimulus. Shows how a computational-efficiency claim is connected to acoustic consequences. Plain specular shoebox image sources are a scoped model, not a complete account of real-room acoustics. Do not add a scattering implementation merely to lengthen this speedrun; state the limitation and test the chosen model carefully.

10.1051/aacus/2024071.note: Examined the abstract, numerical-method discussion and verification setup. Studies spatial/temporal discretization, filtering, dispersion, stability and computation; uses a rigid cubic room, analytical references and a measured BRAS reflection case. The CPU-versus-error discussion explicitly depends on the architecture. Supports a systematic numerical-error paper, provided the error mechanism is characterized and its practical range stated. It does not imply that integer-sample arrival placement is an adequate propagation scheme for a small array.

10.1051/aacus/2026061.relevance: Closest model for a useful bias/tolerance paper
10.1051/aacus/2026061.note: Examined the mismatch derivation, tolerance formulas, validation discussion and conclusions. Derives a dimensionless phase-mismatch index coupling frequency, radius, window length and rotational-speed bias; tests numerical trends and a public fan dataset. Explicitly limits the index's universality and separates primary scaling from secondary influences. This is a good model for turning your error analysis into a bounded practical rule, but its rotating-source formulas and empirical thresholds do not transfer to stationary three-microphone GCC-PHAT. Your native-samples-per-baseline heuristic needs its own derivation and validation.

10.1051/aacus/2026022.note: Examined signal separation, fractional alignment, TDOA/phase estimation and discussion. Shows how secondary arrivals and band-limited temporal smearing alter apparent propagation estimates; compares with a free-field reference and acknowledges geometric/temperature uncertainty. Especially relevant to avoiding an acoustic interpretation of a numerical or processing artifact. Critical caveat: its recovered direct field h3=h1-(h1-h0) is algebraically tied to the reference h0, as the text acknowledges. Do not treat such a construction as an independent ground-truth test or transplant it into your validation.

10.1051/aacus/2023004.relevance: Pair reliability, TDOA and temporal information
10.1051/aacus/2023004.note: Examined the setup and tracking evaluation. Uses image-method reverberation, recorded speech fragments, reliable-pair selection, DUET-derived TDOA and speaker identities in sequential Monte Carlo tracking; the setup states 500 runs unless otherwise noted. Pair confidence and temporal side information already occur in relevant Acta work. Distinguish your static minimal-array error budget from multisource speaker tracking. Its recordings are speech inputs to simulated propagation, not an embedded-board localization validation. Avoid importing its large run count as a universal statistical requirement.

10.1051/aacus/2026076.relevance: Editorial timing and current journal context
10.1051/aacus/2026076.note: Read the editorial. It reports 229 submissions in 2025, a rising rejection rate, and about ten days from submission to reviewer invitation, including preliminary checks. That number is not an acceptance or first-decision promise. It describes the benchmarking topical issue as open at publication, which is not proof of the current deadline. Use for context, not as a personal acceptance probability.

10.1051/aacus/2021034.note: Examined the sensitivity/validation structure, source-identification results and conclusions. The finite-element inverse scheme accounts for boundaries and accurately determined microphone positions; source amplitude and location are not equally well recovered. A favorable virtual microphone configuration is selected using a known simulated field and must be distinguished from the measured configuration. Useful for geometry/model sensitivity and oracle-information controls, but it is not a minimal-array GCC benchmark. Numerical agreement in a favorable synthetic setup cannot substitute for independent measured validation.

10.1051/aacus/2022013.note: Examined acoustic evaluation, results and discussion. Combines DOA probabilities with ASR-derived speech quality across anechoic/reverberant scenes and localized/diffuse noise. Notes cases where adding DOA information can reduce robustness and where switching strategies would require unavailable scene knowledge. Its generalization, observation-time and real-time limitations are stated explicitly; measured room responses and real speech provide distinct evidence sources. Useful for scenario design, oracle-information controls and bounded claims, but it is not a like-for-like benchmark of your band-limited-noise estimator.

10.1051/aacus/2022032.note: Examined the scene descriptions, decay-metric definitions, data documentation and discussion. Provides underground-station, pub and living-room environments, acoustic geometry/material definitions, source/receiver coordinates and measured impulse-response references. Explains the T30/EDT fitting intervals and the metadata needed to reproduce a scene. Adopt the documentation structure and separate nominal model parameters from acoustic observables. External scene data are an optional later extension; they are not a hidden dependency of this existing-files plan.

10.1051/aacus/2021039.note: Abstract-level relevance: active human sound localization and Bayesian inference are distinct from passive microphone-array direction estimation. Useful for terminology and the role of priors/motion, not as a numerical baseline or an array identifiability theorem.

10.1051/aacus/2023006.note: Abstract-level relevance: models human directional localization using binaural sensory evidence and uncertainty. Do not compare human localization errors to your simulated estimator errors without a shared task and metric. Keep such citations selective rather than padding the acoustics bibliography.

10.1051/aacus/2024051.note: Abstract-level relevance: combines disturbance judgments, sound-event localization/detection and targeted headphone ANC, using two reference microphones for a beamformer. An application example, not evidence for your PSR formula, fault-isolation claims or an achievable three-microphone MCU speedup.

10.1051/aacus/2022040.note: Abstract-level relevance: review organizes recorded spatial-audio reproduction into scene, recording, processing, reproduction and perception/evaluation. Useful for locating array/beamforming literature and keeping acquisition and end-task validation separate. It is a literature map, not original evidence for a reverberation floor in your geometry.

10.1051/aacus/2022052.note: Abstract-level relevance: reconstructs a drone flight path/directivity from a microphone array and tests signal processing on simulated moving monopole/dipole data first. Supports the logic of known-truth synthetic controls, while retaining the distinction between simulation verification and measured validation. Moving-source trajectory recovery is outside the present speedrun.

10.1051/aacus/2026052.note: Abstract-level relevance: a 37-microphone tire/road source-identification study combines finite-element modeling with measured data, initially checks a stationary loudspeaker, and confines identification to tonal high-SNR components. Useful example of a controlled reference and explicit domain limits. Its forward match at measurement microphones must not be mistaken for held-out prediction of a new scene.

10.1051/aacus/2024026.note: Abstract-level relevance: drone auralization provides model coefficients and calibration information for reproducibility. Illustrates why a source distribution needs documentation. Your 300–3400 Hz filtered noise remains band-limited noise and should not be described as validated natural speech or drone sound.

10.1051/aacus/2023056.note: Abstract-level relevance: telecommunications review identifies 300–3400 Hz as the historical narrow speech-transmission band and discusses broader spatial/IoT acoustics. The band label does not make noise within that band a speech corpus. Cite only if this historical bandwidth choice is relevant to the final study.

10.1051/aacus/2025010.note: Read the abstract, introduction and concluding discussion in the publisher PDF; visually checked the first and concluding pages. Polack revisits reverberation formulas using free-path statistics, enclosure shape and ergodicity. Concludes that Sabine and Eyring are approximations, with proposed refinements also having domain limits. Supports treating requested RT60 as a model input rather than a guaranteed realized decay. It neither supplies a three-microphone DoA error law nor removes the need to inspect your actual RIRs.

10.1051/aacus/2026090.note: Crossref supplies this record, but both its primary publisher URL and canonical DOI redirect lead to a publisher Content not found page as checked on 7 September 2026. Its publication status is unresolved; it is excluded from the 398 published-volume items. Do not infer that it is published or claim its full text was reviewed.

10.1051/aacus/2026084.note: The publisher DOI landing page was checked and identifies this as a forthcoming article. Kept outside the 398 published-volume items. Its full-sphere human-localization Bayesian model is a scope-boundary reference, not a benchmark of this project's microphone estimator.
